title: Nonuniqueness of percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
main_claim: For every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, T_{p_c} is bounded on l^2(V), so p_c < p_{2->2} <= p_u (Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness and Hutchcroft's operator conjecture). There is also a coupled interval [p1,p2] on which infinitely many infinite clusters exist simultaneously.

issues.description: The nonunimodular case is handed off entirely to an external result, cited as [Hutchcroft2019, Theorem 2.9], giving p_c < p_{q->q}. I could not check offline that the theorem number and its exact operator-norm form match. This is a citation check only; it is not a mathematical gap.
issues.evidence: 'its quasi-transitive action satisfies the hypotheses of [Theorem 2.9]{Hutchcroft2019}, which gives p_c<p_{q->q} for every 1<q<infinity'

coverage: I read every proof section in full: preliminaries, goodness, amplification, moments, trace, deformation, paths and conclusion. I skimmed the consequences section, which only derives corollaries from cited results. Checks done step by step: (1) The ghost-field pivotal moment bounds: the score identity E[Z1_E]=(1-p)E[D_p 1_E], the choice of lambda, the recursion over binomial moments, and the exponent arithmetic in the capped pivotal-radius tail, which works out to X/(8C sqrt(2b)). (2) The configuration-change cost in the good-cluster lemma, including the bound K<=M^{1-s}. (3) Splicing geometry: indices increase, each later piece touches only its predecessor, and seams stay bridges. (4) The inverse-code bound W^k, using goodness to get l_i<=1+K_i M^s. (5) Mean kernel F/b0=(B_n/b_n)(K^k)^T, using column sums equal to one from mass transport. (6) The three classes of the second moment: no-switch, where L_0<=2u^k; nested or adjacent, with N_v endpoints; and disjoint non-adjacent, with the joint-undo injectivity, the replay argument and the trajectory-hit transport. (7) Truncation and the iteration contraction t'/H' <= c_xi t/H. (8) The maximal-potential lemma, the deleted-domain map inequality, the diagonal-loss transport identity, the lower bound D(p) >= chi^{-gamma}, and the likelihood-ratio transcript comparison. (9) The decision-tree (OSSS) proof of chi <= (p_c-p)^{-1-eta}, including the integral exponent (1-a)/a. (10) Trace bound: contact-score concentration, the identity S_full - S_ext = -p k_e, the square bound a6 <= m^3 a3, and the exponents A*, B* at their limiting values. (11) Deformation: edge-weight bound, calibration c(w)P(Q_w)=mu, the BK norm bound 2t T0 P^k T0, the deletion and correlation lemmas, two-leg decomposition, and tr(P^k T0^3) <= rho^k a3. (12) Schramm-lemma smoothing via positive-semidefinite Cauchy–Schwarz and the trace bound, the labeled reversal and domination in the path selection, and the collision sums. (13) Final parameter bookkeeping: k=o(S), B* rho^k -> 0, t* j c_k = o(1), and the resulting contradiction (kR)^2 <= C. I found no unjustified step, sign error or constant error. Circular dependence is excluded: (21) -> (22) -> (23) -> conclusion, with no reverse use.
sibling_notes: Family 214 had no prior entries on the board when I checked. Lemmas likely reusable by companion papers: the deletion-uniform good-cluster tail (eq. 6), the critical fractional moments for alpha<1/2 (eq. 21), and the near-linear susceptibility bound (eq. 22).
